title: Why Zenefits repriced shares: a fraud settlement
why: Repricing works as a de facto settlement: undisclosed compliance fraud makes prior-round purchases securities fraud, so the valuation is corrected toward what it should have been.

title: Why language string representations age badly
why: Languages designed when Unicode fit in 65536 characters chose 2-byte encodings, the worst of both worlds; UTF-8 is the modern choice, and C strings already fit it well.

title: Hidden costs of splitting a monolith into services
why: Services talking JSON add serialization overhead, painful cross-repo branching and builds, and new auth complexity that a single monolith never had.

title: Skipping a grade: a personal regret
why: The author skipped a grade and entered college too young, missing lessons in growing up; taking a year off might have served better.

title: How a photo startup squeezed its AWS costs
why: Insider account of cutting cloud spend by optimizing S3, EC2 and RDS, and the argument that large photo platforms run their own storage at scale.

title: Snopes kept a wrong supporting fact
why: A podiatrist showed a fact Snopes used to debunk a myth was false, and Snopes kept it anyway; anecdote about one article, not a general lesson.

title: Argument that non-ionising radiation may cause cancer
why: Opinion arguing against scientific dogma without specific mechanisms or evidence; mostly a complaint about dismissive experts.

title: List of June 2023 Reddit protest threads
why: Moderator-style list of linked discussion threads about the Reddit API changes; navigational, with no standalone lesson.

title: Cowboys versus architects in programming
why: A loosely argued taxonomy of programmer styles that mostly voices opinion about agile and unit testing without substantive evidence.

title: Free speech and workplace heresies
why: Political argument about speech, firing and the left and right, with no technical or informational content.

title: Health care as a consumer product
why: Political opinion on American versus European health care, offering comparisons without a substantive mechanism or analysis.

title: Defending moderation of a coding bootcamp subreddit
why: A moderator's defense in a dispute about a competitor; a moderation note specific to one case, with no general lesson.

title: Complaints about large iPhones
why: Emotional rant about phone size and Apple's product direction, with no technical explanation or lesson.

title: Apple's absence from a Yahoo article
why: Rebuttal opinion about Apple's hiring and culture versus the article's thesis; argumentative and not informational.

title: The financial trajectory of a scientist
why: A quoted career timeline makes a sharp point about academic precarity, but it is a rhetorical complaint rather than a lesson a technical reader would take away.

title: Why money beats punishment for unpleasant chores
why: Without money, societies rely on punishment for undesirable work; communes collapse when unpaid people quit, while prices adjust small mismatches smoothly.

title: CNN's decline into clickbait
why: General complaint about news quality, incentives and Reddit-driven news, without specific evidence or an explanatory model.

title: Why personal cars beat transit for many trips
why: Cars win on near-zero waiting, proportional lateness penalty, night and weather availability, and direct routes; cutting parking alone will not shift trips.

title: Interview difficulty rising at big tech
why: A candidate's frustrated account of hard coding rounds; first-hand, but it is a complaint about hiring rather than a technical lesson.

title: Reversed index column order makes inserts far slower
why: Two identically filled MySQL tables with reversed composite-index order: one loads in 25 minutes, the other takes over 37 hours, with matching checksums.

title: Automatic scale tracking helps weight loss
why: Personal weight-loss account; the useful idea is trend-line tracking, but it stays anecdotal and largely reports the author's own experience.

title: Media coverage of Portland protests
why: Political argument about news coverage and protest groups, with claims not supported by data or a technical lesson.

title: Managers and remote workers living abroad
why: Manager anecdotes mixing tax, legal and political opinions about remote workers abroad; not a clear, substantive explanation.

title: Baptism by fire as a junior engineer
why: A personal story of sink-or-swim onboarding and pride in growth; it reports experience but offers no transferable explanation.

title: Skepticism about statistical theories of the brain
why: Opinion arguing that single-theory brain science is implausible, supported by bias lists and an anecdote, with no new explanation.

title: Skepticism about statistical theories of the brain
why: Opinion arguing that single-theory brain science is implausible, supported by bias lists and an anecdote, with no new explanation.

title: Questions about FCC and rogue satellites
why: A list of speculative questions about regulation, cubesat inspection and orbital spying; provocative but explains nothing on its own.

title: Why maintainers resent unpaid open source
why: Opinion about open source burnout and expectations of payment; sympathetic, but without concrete practical or technical content.

title: How DynamoDB really stores data internally
why: Insider: hash keys map to three-replica quorum groups with one master for writes; underneath, the storage is many MySQL instances with JNI bridges, not LevelDB.

title: A Silicon Valley startup that ran out of money
why: A first-hand account of a fraud-like funding story; a cautionary personal narrative with no transferable technical lesson.

title: The fallacy behind bitcoin's hopes
why: Argument that bitcoin believers' scenarios imply a catastrophe, so its success is unlikely; a sharp point but mostly opinion about a market.

title: Running at scale without containers, using Nix
why: Containers give reproducible deployments but not builds; Nix pins full build dependencies, and Kubernetes mostly helps stateless apps, not databases.

title: Hackers as the new privileged class
why: Polemic about hacker identity and privilege, with rhetorical flourishes but no technical content or evidence.

title: Why word processors need custom text layout
why: Word processors need layout details browsers do not expose, like bidi selection geometry and reflowing only the current line while typing, so apps render text on canvas.

title: What YC equity actually buys
why: Opinion about YC's value and the access to VCs it sells; argues from valuations rather than teaching a technical or practical point.

title: AlphaGo's edge-case play and optimization
why: Strong optimizers pick strategies that look balanced to humans while shrinking the opponent's win probability; optimal solutions often sit at extreme corners of the space.

title: Mocking a Plan 9 desktop guide
why: Snarky critique of a retro operating system guide, with jokes and sarcasm rather than explanation or practical value.

title: Why banks keep legacy password systems
why: Legacy vendor systems often cannot add salted hashes; banks lean on second factors and network isolation, since rebuilding risks outages that could outweigh the gain.

title: Why the author dislikes Vue after React
why: Opinionated framework rant with one concrete example of dynamic component rendering; the argument is mostly preference rather than teachable explanation.

title: Wait before extracting repeated code
why: Duplication that looks identical may be incidental; keep it until changes reveal the true shared shape, then refactor when a bug shows the same edit is needed in many places.

title: SR-71 engineering: leaking fuel and fitting panels
why: The SR-71 leaked fuel on the ground so its panels could stretch and seal at speed; many parts failed, showing that effectiveness can beat minimalism.

title: Why aviation and clock speeds stalled
why: Aviation hit limits from burning fuel and CPU clocks plateaued near 3-4 GHz at atomic-scale limits; both fields saw progress stall after decades of rapid gains.

title: Incremental grades create stress
why: Teacher and lawyer experience suggests high-stakes incremental grading causes panic; a reasonable opinion on assessment design, not a technical explanation.

title: Ranked tips for better sleep
why: Consistent bed and wake times matter most, then morning outdoor light, dim evenings, passive pre-bed routines and nasal breathing, ranked by the author's experience.

title: Insider account of Optimizely's decline
why: Abandoning self-serve for vague enterprise sales, opaque marketing and extractive pricing eroded a hot startup's value, as seen from inside.

title: Inequality is not the problem
why: Political economy opinion arguing that inequality is harmless absent rent-seeking; a debate position with no new data.

title: Copilot and what grading should measure
why: Opinion about whether coding tests and university grading still make sense when AI can write code; a debate, not a lesson.

title: A cracked OLED laptop lid
why: A personal complaint about a broken laptop screen and build quality, with no general lesson beyond the author's bad experience.

title: Why verification was Twitter's real value
why: Opinion that identity verification underpinned Twitter's value and that Musk misjudged it; persuasive but argumentative rather than explanatory.

title: Why Famo.us prioritized performance over basics
why: Insider rationale: targeting native-level performance from the start leaves developers headroom, so the team traded basic web-app features for speed.

title: Live video latency: why MJPEG won
why: HLS-style streaming hit 7-second latency and WebRTC looked unfinished, so the author chose low-latency Motion JPEG to get under one second on a LAN.

title: Personal favorite purchases
why: A list of personal product picks such as earplugs and bone-conduction headphones; subjective recommendations with little explanation.

title: Show door-to-door time to nudge travelers
why: Policy opinion that airlines should show total city-to-city time and cost; a useful framing, but mainly an argument for a regulatory change.

title: Unanswered questions about Unicode handling
why: A list of unresolved questions about encodings, BOMs and right-to-left text with no answers; complaint rather than explanation.

title: How spreadsheet-driven cost cuts eroded culture
why: A former CEO saw PE analysts cut what was easy to measure, like benefits, while the morale and performance costs of those cuts stayed hard to quantify.

title: What makes API reference pages scannable
why: Good reference pages group methods by purpose, summarize each group up top, and use layout and color to separate signature parts; Rust's string page does none of these.

title: Living well on little money
why: Personal lifestyle reflection on money, work hours and happiness; a personal choice story with no transferable technical lesson.

title: Skepticism about Cargo and Windows support
why: Opinion arguing Rust and its package manager neglect Windows; a platform flame without substantive technical analysis.

title: Frustrations with macOS reliability
why: A long list of personal complaints about macOS crashes, sleep and tooling; venting rather than explaining causes or fixes.

title: Why remote browser isolation breaks screen readers
why: Rendering pages inert for security removes what screen readers depend on; dynamic pages make a general fix hard, so the tradeoff is genuinely difficult.

title: Non-jokes and performance in poetry slams
why: Reflective musing on delivery in jokes and poetry; amusing and thoughtful, but with no concrete technical or factual lesson.

title: Prompting GPT-3 with an internal monologue
why: Asking GPT-3 to write a parenthetical reasoning step before answering helped it recognize nonsense questions and give more accurate, hedged answers.

title: Chinese companies as tools of statecraft
why: In China the state, military and corporations are one entity, so treating firms like Huawei as market competitors misreads them as instruments of statecraft.

title: Lament for open standards on the web
why: Nostalgic opinion that the web drifted into walled gardens and that chat lacks an open standard; sentiment without a mechanism or practical guide.

title: Lorentzian manifolds: signature and curvature
why: A Lorentzian metric usually has signature (1, n-1); flat Minkowski space is not hyperbolic space, which has constant negative curvature, so the two cannot be the same.

title: Physical work and job satisfaction
why: Personal reflection contrasting bakery work with office work; evocative, but mostly an essay about meaning without an explanatory lesson.

title: Income growth lags house prices
why: Opinion with FRED data about income and housing prices; plausible concern, but mostly personal worry rather than teachable analysis.

title: Tall passengers and economy seats
why: A complaint about airline seat pitch for tall passengers; a personal grievance with no broader explanation.

title: Why Munich's LiMux migration struggled
why: Insider notes: aging desktops with 256 MB RAM swapped constantly, slow SDSL site links and immature office software made the Linux migration look worse than its causes.

title: Hiring household staff in Mexico City
why: A personal lifestyle account of cheap live-in help abroad; anecdotal, with no lesson beyond the author's own arrangement.

title: What ruins a SaaS demo for buyers
why: IT buyers want live feature demos, technically fluent presenters, relevant use cases and clear security answers; slides and vague security claims kill a sale.

title: Why many patents are mere implementations
why: Judged by skilled-in-the-art standards, many patents only apply obvious implementations that engineers reach independently, so obviousness tests are applied too loosely.

title: Leaving Apple over binary monitoring
why: A customer's ultimatum to Apple about app monitoring and ecosystem lock-in; opinion and threat, not an explanation of how it works.

title: Living in a van without a home
why: Personal account of living homeless in a van; moving and human, but a first-person story rather than a teachable technical or practical lesson.

title: Knuth vs McIlroy: the famous word-frequency duel
why: Knuth wrote a literate program for word frequency and McIlroy answered with a Unix pipeline; the criticism was unfair because Knuth wrote the program he was asked for.

title: Predicting AI will replace software engineers
why: Speculative prediction that AI will eliminate most engineering jobs, with no evidence or technical detail beyond the author's expectation.

title: Why youtube-dl's community matters more than code
why: Opinion that a takedown cannot be fixed by cloned software because the community that responded to site changes is gone.

title: Collapsing a server stack into one executable
why: Replacing TCP with UDP, bypassing the kernel for Ethernet and using memory-mapped lmdb reads let a startup serve reads in under 3 microseconds.

title: Google's stance on webmaster phone support
why: A corporate PR reply about support channels and an appeal; reassurance and policy talk, not a substantive technical explanation.

title: Nostalgia about early programming tedium
why: Recollections of punch cards, core dumps and hostile media about software careers; vivid memories but mainly anecdote with no clear lesson.

title: Software freedom versus physical tools
why: A screwdriver analogy for software licenses argues against moral framing of copyleft; a persuasive opinion, not a substantive technical explanation.

title: Levandowski and the future-only mindset
why: Commentary on a controversial figure and a quote dismissing history; opinion about a person rather than a lesson.

title: Defending Apple's iBooks Author license
why: Licensing opinion that free-for-noncommercial tools carry costs and restrictions; a debate position with little new technical information.

title: Why SCADA systems need one-way data diodes
why: Industrial control systems send data two ways to IT historians; software rules alone cannot stop backward flow, so physical one-way data diodes are the verifiable fix.

title: How consultancies and legacy companies fail projects
why: Satirical account of consultants and corporate IT dysfunction; amusing and familiar, but anecdotal rather than a clear, transferable explanation.

title: Why rich nations lose drive
why: Speculative essay that complacency causes national decline and suggests wars refresh countries; opinion about history without evidence.

title: Static type checking versus tests
why: Opinion that compile-time checks beat defensive code and tests in dynamic languages; a reasonable position but with little new substance.

title: How Google projects start as grassroots efforts
why: A Google engineer defends AngularDart as organic grassroots work; useful insider context, but mostly a rebuttal of skeptics.

title: Scammed through Amazon's support transfer
why: A personal scam-call story about support transfers and a fake technician; a warning anecdote without a broader practical guide.

title: Companies should own open source dependency risk
why: Opinion that companies using unvetted open source should bear liability like negligent restaurants; a policy argument, not a how-to.

title: Robotaxis will reduce congestion
why: Speculative argument that robotaxis and congestion pricing will fix traffic; forecasts and opinion rather than evidence or an explanation.

title: A paid Linux distribution for funding
why: Product idea that a subscription Linux could fund UX and upstream fixes; a proposal and opinion, not an explanation of a technique.

title: The personal cost of bootstrapping a startup
why: Personal account of losing savings and a codebase while bootstrapping; a cautionary story with limited transferable explanation.

title: Learn ML by modifying working GitHub code
why: Skip courses at first: pick a problem, find a GitHub model that solves a similar one, run and modify it, then look up concepts as they block you.

title: Living without work and following interests
why: Personal reflection on dropping structured work for spontaneous interests; a lifestyle story with no transferable technique.

title: Space journalism's anecdote-first template
why: Meta-commentary noting that space articles open with human anecdotes before science; a critique of writing style, not a technical lesson.

title: Consequences of cancelling poor citizens' debt
why: Economic argument that debt cancellation would cut lending and raise rates; plausible reasoning but mainly a policy opinion without data.

title: Public funding for drug development
why: Advocacy for public drug development and capped insulin prices, citing sources; a policy position rather than an explanation.

title: Doubts about Snowden's claims
why: Political opinion questioning Snowden's motives and claims; argumentative and not informational.

title: Rebuttal of Rust complaints for codec work
why: Point-by-point rebuttal of a codec developer's Rust complaints; some substance on explicit casts, but it reads as a reply that only makes sense in context.
